Disclosure to Promote the Right To Information 

Whereas the Parliament of India has set out to provide a practical regime of right to 
information for citizens to secure access to information under the control of public authorities, 
in order to promote transparency and accountability in the working of every public authority, 
and whereas the attached publication of the Bureau of Indian Standards is of particular interest 
to the public, particularly disadvantaged communities and those engaged in the pursuit of 
education and knowledge, the attached public safety standard is made available to promote the 
timely dissemination of this information in an accurate manner to the public.

IS : 10963 -1984 




Indian Standard 

SPECIFICATION FOR 
FORCEPS, HOOF TESTING 



( Reaffirmed 2006 ) 



1. Scope — Covers requirements for forceps, hoof testing used in veterinary surgery. 

2. Shape and Dimensions — As given in Fig. 1, 




All dimensions in millimetres. 
FIG. 1 FORCEPS, HOOF TESTING 

2.1 To/erances — Coarse class of 18:2102-1969 'Specification for allowable deviations for 
dimensions without specified tolerances ( first revision ) \ 



3. Materials 

Components 

Screw 



Stainless steel conforming to designation 20Cr13 or 
30Cr13 of IS : 6603-1972 ' Specification for stainless 
steel bars and flats '. 

The screw shall be of the same material as used 
for forceps. 



4. Manufacture, Workmanship and Finish 

4.1 Forceps shall be free from pits, burrs, cracks, flaws and all other surface defects. 

4.2 The knurling on the jaws shall be well defined and without pitting. 

4.3 The edges, except for knurling shall be even, rounded and nowhere sharp. 



Adopted 23 July 1984 



© September 1984 ISI 



Gr 1 



INDIAN STANDARDS INSTITUTION 
MANAK BHAVAN, 9 BAHADUR SHAH ZAFAR MARG 
NEW DELHI 110002 



18:10963-1984 

4.4 With the handles open at 20*, there shall be no undue play at the joint. There shall be no undue 

stiffness. 

4.5 The forceps shall be passivated and polished bright. 

5. Hardness — 400 to 500 HV tested in accordance with IS : 1501-1968 ' Method for Vickers hardness 
test for steel ( first revision ) \ 

6. Tests 

6.1 Functional Test — A piece of mild steel flat 3 mm thick shall be placed between the jaws. The 
handle shall be pressed firmly together with one hand and an attempt shall be made with the other 
to remove the mild steel flat. The flat shall not be easily pulled. The forceps on opening shall not 
show any sign of damage. 

6-1.1 A block of hard wood 20 mm thick shall be placed between the knurled jaws of the forceps. 
A load of 45 kg shall be applied gradually to the tips of the handles ( 22'5 kg on each handle ) and 
allowed to act for 2 min. On completion of the test, the forceps shall show no sign of damage. 

6.2 Corrosion Resistance — The forceps shall pass the test given in IS : 7531-1975' Method for boiling 
and autoclaving test for corrosion resistance of stainless steel surgical instruments '. 

7. Marking — The forceps shall be legibly and indelibly stamped with the manufacturer's name, 
initials or recognized trade-mark, year of manufacture and words ' stainless steel ' or letters 'SS '. 

7.1 ISI Certification Marking — Details available with the Indian Standards Institution. 

8. Packing — As specified in the contract or order. 



Printed at New India Printing Press. Khur|a. India
